current.text: Most experts expect Neemias Queta to start at center and Robinson to come off the bench. Karalis picked Robinson to start but admitted Queta will probably start.
He is projected for only 55 to 60 games at about 22 minutes per game.
Boston has 16 back-to-backs, tied for the most in the league.
He is expected to sit every back-to-back, so Boston's heavy back-to-back schedule hits him harder than most players.
Boston plays 4, 3 and 4 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21, one game short of the maximum, with three back-to-backs in that window.
Boston's rotation is very deep, with at least 12 rotation-level players, so bench minutes are spread thin.
Do not spend a draft pick on him at his Yahoo ADP of 108. Treat him as a category-league streamer and check his back-to-backs first.
He is a good stash where stashing is easy, because he might win the starting job or Queta might get hurt.

durable.text: His value comes from FG%, rebounds and blocks only, in limited minutes.
He is one of the worst free throw shooters in the league. His 40.8% last season was the worst among top 200 players and one of the worst FT impacts.
He has no shooting range, makes no threes and scores only about 6 points per game.
He plays as a pick-and-roll lob threat and dunker-spot big who gives vertical spacing.
Ankle problems and foul trouble limit his minutes, and he has a history of missed games. He cannot play back-to-backs.

note: Yahoo ranks him 176th with a value of 0 USD. ESPN has him 116th at 2 USD. Both sit near or past our 144-player draft pool, so he is at most a 1 USD final pick for a punt FT% team that wants FG%, rebounds and blocks. A better plan is to leave him on waivers and stream him on days when Boston does not play a back-to-back. Early in the season, check whether he or Queta starts and whether his minutes rise above about 22. A Queta injury would make him a quick pickup.
